correctness.rationale: The proof was independently reconstructed from the exact RESULT.md. With \(a=x^2,b=y^2,c=z^2\), \(R^2=S\), \(r^2=abc/P\), and the edge definition gives \(q=1-3P/S^2\). Normalizing \(S=1\) reduces the fixed-\(q\) locus to a circle; the stated trigonometric parameterization gives \(p_1p_2p_3=(1-3q+2q^{3/2}\cos3\theta)/27\). Positivity permits the full cosine range exactly for \(\sqrt q<1/2\), and thereafter cuts the lower endpoint to an unattained zero while preserving the upper two-equal branch. A fresh independent 5,000-sample computation verified the bound throughout random positive coordinate triples; the package verifier was also read but is only corroborative.
